lines.text: Well. The one who walked up from the Low Ford at dawn. Chid came in babbling about blue lights going out at the crossing, and here you are, bleeding on my step. I'm Rook. This is the Last Lamp. Sit down before you fall down.

segments.text: Well. The one who walked up from the Low Ford at dawn. Chid came in babbling about blue lights going out at the crossing, and here you are, bleeding on my step. I'm Rook. This is the Last Lamp. Sit down before you fall down.

direction.intent: takes charge of a bloodied stranger
direction.wants: to take charge of you, and to see who you are
direction.hides: Vonnra pays her for news of Low Ford arrivals, double for this one
direction.note: 'Well.' a beat, looking you over. On the Chid sentence she watches your face for how you take 'blue lights going out'. A dry edge on 'bleeding on my step'. No laugh at the end: a breath, and the warmth is in the order itself.

lines.text: Nothing you don't know already, pet; you did half of it. Holloway's counting what's left, Harlan's counting what came back, and the Penhales say their dog won't go in the barn any more. Stands at the door and whines at the floor, and won't be told.

segments.text: Nothing you don't know already, pet; you did half of it. Holloway's counting what's left, Harlan's counting what came back, and the Penhales say their dog won't go in the barn any more. Stands at the door and whines at the floor, and won't be told.

direction.intent: the town's news, and a strange dog
direction.note: Wry tally of who's counting what. The dog story slows and darkens: 'whines at the floor' uneasy; 'won't be told' firm.

lines.text: Wenna says the stream's running clean. The wolves have gone quiet, and Holloway's sulking because there's nobody left to pay. Harlan's still asking after his boy, mind.

segments.text: Wenna says the stream's running clean. The wolves have gone quiet, and Holloway's sulking because there's nobody left to pay. Harlan's still asking after his boy, mind.

direction.note: Pleased; mock-scorn on Holloway sulking. 'mind' Yorkshire, a gentle reminder.

lines.text: No wolves on the road now. None. Brannoc's never seen so many pelts, and Maeca hasn't been in since. Make of that what you like. Harlan's still asking after his boy.

segments.text: No wolves on the road now. None. Brannoc's never seen so many pelts, and Maeca hasn't been in since. Make of that what you like. Harlan's still asking after his boy.

direction.note: 'None.' flat and pointed. 'Make of that what you like.' cool.

lines.text: The wolves are settled, one way or another, and nobody's thanked anybody for it, which is how you know it's settled. Harlan's still asking after his boy, mind. And Jessop, the toll clerk, owes me for three rounds and hasn't been back to pay.

segments.text: The wolves are settled, one way or another, and nobody's thanked anybody for it, which is how you know it's settled. Harlan's still asking after his boy, mind. And Jessop, the toll clerk, owes me for three rounds and hasn't been back to pay.

direction.note: Dry wit on 'which is how you know it's settled'. Grievance on Jessop's unpaid rounds.

lines.text: Jory Coyle's home, asleep in my good room with the lamp lit, and Harlan's been up my stairs four times to look at him. The wolves are another matter: Holloway's paying for pelts, Maeca says they're sick, and the Penhale boy says they drink from the stream and fall down. Pick one.

direction.note: Warmth for Jory; exasperated fondness for Harlan. 'Pick one.' dry.

lines.text: Harlan's shut his shutters and won't open the door, not even to me. And the wolves are still at it: Holloway's paying for pelts, Maeca says they're sick. Don't ask me which. I've stopped asking.

lines.text: Wolves, mainly. Holloway's paying for pelts, Maeca says they're sick, Harlan says they ate his caravan, and the Coyle boy's still missing. And Jessop, the toll clerk, was buying rounds at the Flagon like he'd come into money, the night the wagons went. Pick a story.

lines.text: Three roads meet here, and everyone on them stops at my door. South's the Low Ford. East's the Old Road and the Verge. North's shut, and a girl in shiny armour will tell you why, at length. Everybody else you'll meet whether you want to or not.

lines.text: You found old Ashe, and his trunk. Captain of the first Watch, when it was forty lamps and not four. This inn's named for his: the Last Lamp, because it was the last one lit the night they closed the north road. We light the hearth from it every winter. Keep what was in the trunk; he'd have wanted it used. Just leave him where he lies.

lines.text: Off in the Hollow the Pack is loud, a long tangle of voices, and she stops with her hands on your buckle and listens, and then she laughs: a short surprised sound, as if she'd trodden on something. "They're eating." She pulls you down onto the hides. Her hands are hard and careful, the way they are with a snare, and then they're not careful. The fire goes down to embers. Neither of you feeds it. Later, under the hides, she sleeps like a hunter: lightly, one hand on the crossbow and the other on you.

lines.text: The water's gone cool by the time either of you notices, and she drags the quilt off the bed and onto the floor rather than walk three steps. She is slower tonight. She keeps a hand flat on you the whole time, the way you'd keep a hand on a horse you'd been told was skittish, and when you look at her she says, "Don't," and kisses you so you can't. After, you lie on the floor of the blue room with the lamp turned down to a bead, and she doesn't get up to dress, and you don't ask why. You wake with her hair across your chest and the sun already up. She is dressed, and counting, and she counts it twice.

lines.text: She laughs when the water slops over the side, and again when you try to mop it with her shift. Then the lamp is down to a bead, and the blue room is a small warm place with the whole night outside it. She talks the way she always talks, low against your ear, telling you exactly what she means to do next and then doing it, and she's good at it and likes it and makes no secret of either. But there are gaps, tonight. Places where she stops mid-sentence and doesn't finish, and you don't need her to. You wake with her hair across your chest and the sun already up. She is dressed, and counting.

lines.text: She doesn't talk the way she talks for money. She doesn't talk at all, at first. She undresses you as if she's never done it before, which is absurd, and she knows it's absurd, and halfway through she laughs into your neck and can't stop. Then she does stop, and the laugh goes somewhere else. She's slower than on her working nights, and less sure, and once she stops altogether with her forehead against yours and just breathes, and you wait, and she goes on. The lamp burns down on its own. Nobody turns it. In the dark, much later, she says into your shoulder, "You told me anyway," and nothing else, and then she sleeps.

lines.text: You roll them down into the ravine's water one at a time, and listen to each one not go off.

segments.text: You roll them down into the ravine's water one at a time, and listen to each one not go off.

direction.intent: to let the relief arrive in the silence
direction.wants: to let the relief arrive in the silence
direction.note: 'One at a time' slow; 'not go off' flat and quiet.

lines.text: The fuse fizzes. You have a few seconds. Run.

segments.text: The fuse fizzes. You have a few seconds. Run.

direction.note: Tight and quick; 'Run.' short, not shouted.

lines.text: The fragment fits one notch of the seven, and under your hand the whole sigil wakes, violet, like an eye opening. The door is listening.

segments.text: The fragment fits one notch of the seven, and under your hand the whole sigil wakes, violet, like an eye opening. The door is listening.

direction.note: 'like an eye opening' slower; a pause before 'The door is listening.'
direction.beats: The fragment fits one notch of the seven, and under your hand the whole sigil wakes, violet, like an eye opening. [beat] The door is listening.

lines.text: The fragment fits one notch of the seven, and the stone warms under it. Whatever the sigil is waiting for, it is not daylight.

segments.text: The fragment fits one notch of the seven, and the stone warms under it. Whatever the sigil is waiting for, it is not daylight.

direction.note: Plain; the last clause level.

lines.text: Old-empire script over the door: "Here the Seventh Legion buried what it could not burn." Below it, a sigil with seven notches, all empty.

segments.text: Old-empire script over the door. Here the Seventh Legion buried what it could not burn. Below it, a sigil with seven notches, all empty.

direction.note: The inscription read slowly as old written words; 'all empty' quiet.
direction.say: Old-empire script over the door. Here the Seventh Legion buried what it could not burn. Below it, a sigil with seven notches, all empty.

lines.text: A door of black stone, smooth as glass. Cut over it, words in a dead tongue: HIC LEGIO SEPTIMA SEPELIVIT QUOD URERE NON POTUIT. Under them, a violet sigil you cannot read. It hums against your teeth.

segments.text: A door of black stone, smooth as glass. Cut over it, words in a dead tongue: hic legio septima sepelivit quod urere non potuit. Under them, a violet sigil you cannot read. It hums against your teeth.

direction.say: A door of black stone, smooth as glass. Cut over it, words in a dead tongue: hic legio septima sepelivit quod urere non potuit. Under them, a violet sigil you cannot read. It hums against your teeth.
direction.note: The Latin said slowly, as old words.

lines.text: In the bones of one hand, a wedge of black stone cut to fit something.

segments.text: In the bones of one hand, a wedge of black stone cut to fit something.

direction.note: Plain.

lines.text: The skull turns, very slightly, toward you.

segments.text: The skull turns, very slightly, toward you.

direction.note: A hush: one of his four whispers.

lines.text: It was never locked from the outside.

segments.text: It was never locked from the outside.

lines.text: Bootprints in the mud, fresh, going up to the door. None coming away. Trodden into one heel-print: a copper toll-token, stamped with three roads.

segments.text: Bootprints in the mud, fresh, going up to the door. None coming away. Trodden into one heel-print: a copper toll-token, stamped with three roads.

direction.intent: someone went in and did not come out
direction.note: The token a careful find; a pause before 'None coming away.'
direction.beats: Bootprints in the mud, fresh, going up to the door. [beat] None coming away. Trodden into one heel-print: a copper toll-token, stamped with three roads.

lines.text: Under the brambles, where the wolves go when one of them is dying: a circlet of moonsilver, cold as snow.

segments.text: Under the brambles, where the wolves go when one of them is dying: a circlet of moonsilver, cold as snow.

direction.intent: a treasure where wolves go to die
direction.note: Slow; 'cold as snow' no softer than the rest.

lines.text: A teamster, thin and grey, stumbles out and grips your arm. His nails are broken to the quick from the bars.

segments.text: A teamster, thin and grey, stumbles out and grips your arm. His nails are broken to the quick from the bars.

direction.note: Plain; the nails are the detail.

lines.text: A woman who will not stop saying thank you.

segments.text: A woman who will not stop saying thank you.

direction.note: Plain.

lines.text: A young man, freckled, still holding the bars after the door is open.

segments.text: A young man, freckled, still holding the bars after the door is open.

direction.note: Plain.

lines.text: Jory. Jory Coyle. Is my uncle—? Is he—?

segments.text: Jory. Jory Coyle. Is my uncle... Is he...

direction.say: Jory. Jory Coyle. Is my uncle... Is he...

lines.text: Something snaps inside the pump with a sound like a bone. The wheel stops. The slurry stops.

segments.text: Something snaps inside the pump with a sound like a bone. The wheel stops. The slurry stops.

direction.note: Each stopping its own short sentence.

lines.text: When the dust comes down, the hillside is a wound. Small shapes crawl out of it with their lamps still lit. Some of them are on fire. Most of them do not crawl far.

segments.text: When the dust comes down, the hillside is a wound. Small shapes crawl out of it with their lamps still lit. Some of them are on fire. Most of them do not crawl far.

direction.note: Level and quiet throughout, 'Most of them do not crawl far.' included.

lines.text: The fire takes the tents, and then the cages. There is screaming, and the smell, and hands through the bars; and then there is only the fire.

segments.text: The fire takes the tents, and then the cages. There is screaming, and the smell, and hands through the bars; and then there is only the fire.

direction.note: Level; a pause before 'and then there is only the fire', said low.

lines.text: The brambles go up like paper. Beyond them, a glade full of pale light.

segments.text: The brambles go up like paper. Beyond them, a glade full of pale light.

direction.note: Quick on the fire, slower on the glade.

lines.text: You hack a way through the brambles. Beyond them, a glade full of pale light.

segments.text: You hack a way through the brambles. Beyond them, a glade full of pale light.

direction.note: The effort, then slower on the glade.

lines.text: Four grey shapes fall in beside you at the edge of the wood.

segments.text: Four grey shapes fall in beside you at the edge of the wood.

direction.note: Still and slow.

lines.text: Where you fell. The ground has kept your things for you, most of them.

segments.text: Where you fell. The ground has kept your things for you, most of them.

direction.note: Plain; 'most of them' level.

lines.text: OI! No surface-meat past the pump!

segments.text: OI! No surface-meat past the pump!

direction.note: Squeaky shout.

lines.text: The water is a long way down, and clean. Somebody has scratched "M. + J." into the stone.

segments.text: The water is a long way down, and clean. Somebody has scratched M and J into the stone.

direction.intent: a small human mark on the well
direction.note: Read 'M. + J.' as letters: 'em and jay'.
direction.say: The water is a long way down, and clean. Somebody has scratched M and J into the stone.

lines.text: The clerk's key turns sweetly. Inside: crates, dust, and a ledger Pell should have burned.

segments.text: The clerk's key turns sweetly. Inside: crates, dust, and a ledger Pell should have burned.

direction.note: Plain; the ledger line level.

lines.text: The lock gives under your picks. Inside: crates, dust, and a ledger Pell should have burned.

segments.text: The lock gives under your picks. Inside: crates, dust, and a ledger Pell should have burned.

direction.note: Quiet and careful.

lines.text: The whole town is in the Quiet Garden, round a fresh grave beside the old captain's stone. Brannoc kneels at its head with an iron marker and his hammer: three strokes, iron into earth. Rook sets the inn's lamp at its foot, lit, in broad daylight, and steps back, and back.

segments.text: The whole town is in the Quiet Garden, round a fresh grave beside the old captain's stone. Brannoc kneels at its head with an iron marker and his hammer: three strokes, iron into earth. Rook sets the inn's lamp at its foot, lit, in broad daylight, and steps back, and back.

direction.note: Three strokes, each its own beat; 'and steps back, and back.' level.
direction.beats: ...Brannoc kneels at its head with an iron marker and his hammer: three strokes, [beat] iron into earth. [beat] Rook sets the inn's lamp at its foot, lit, in broad daylight, and steps back, [beat] and back.

lines.text: Beside the old captain's stone, sunk in the nettles, a trunk the Watch forgot: ember shards, a purse, and a note: "Keep the lights lit. — C."

segments.text: Beside the old captain's stone, sunk in the nettles, a trunk the Watch forgot: ember shards, a purse, and a note. Keep the lights lit. C.

direction.note: The note read as written words: 'Keep the lights lit.' Then the initial: 'C.'
direction.say: Beside the old captain's stone, sunk in the nettles, a trunk the Watch forgot: ember shards, a purse, and a note. Keep the lights lit. C.

lines.text: The Waystation: walls, smoke, the smell of bread. People stop to look at you. News travels fast here.

segments.text: The Waystation: walls, smoke, the smell of bread. People stop to look at you. News travels fast here.

direction.note: A list of sensations, unhurried; 'News travels fast here.' plain.

lines.text: A cartographer has set up a stall on the Old Road, by the east gate: maps to places the road forgets.

segments.text: A cartographer has set up a stall on the Old Road, by the east gate: maps to places the road forgets.

direction.note: Plain; a slight lift on 'places the road forgets'.
